title: verify:recorder-e2e: 3 Recorder metadata-parity failures after save/restart
description: Full-suite run 2026-08-18: verify:recorder-e2e 58 PASS / 3 FAIL, reproducible on re-run. Failing: 'Recorder locator/value/wait metadata survives initial save', 'Persisted flow still carries Recorder metadata', 'Flow Designer no-op save preserves all Recorder-owned metadata'. Two changes from this session are plausible and must be checked before anything else: eeb7a21 (record independent navigation as a replayable step — changes what actions exist and may shift positional pairing) and 083c34e (fill-echo suppression — changes which fill survives, so a step's valueSource could differ from the captured action at that index). NEXT: dump recorderMetadataFromAction vs recorderMetadataFromStep for each index and diff, rather than reasoning about it; the evidence dir (test-artifacts/recorder-e2e/<ts>/) does not currently carry the captured-action side.
close_reason: FIXED. NOT a regression from this session, and my own bead was wrong to name my two commits as plausible causes — corrected here. The verifier compared a PRE-hash captured action against a POST-hash saved step: buildRecordedFlow hashes identity fingerprints before persisting (FlowProfile.ts: every token is a SHA-256 hash, never raw page text, so it is safe to persist in a saved flow), hashing landed 2026-08-08 in ddd9c84, and this comparison was last reconciled 2026-08-01 in 57dfad2. It has been structurally unsatisfiable since. THREE root causes, found by making the failure self-describing rather than by reasoning: (1) identity.fingerprint is hashed on purpose — now compared THROUGH that transformation via hashFingerprintMirror, which reproduces the product algorithm (sha256 hex sliced to 20, name/text hashed word-wise then deduped and sorted) so equality still fails if a single token changes or stops being hashed; (2) the finalizer legitimately ADDS fields a raw action never had (identity.captureEvidence.pageKey), so 'metadata survives' is now a SUBSET comparison — a claim about loss, not about additions — and stays strict for every recorded key; (3) locator.blueprintCapture is a consumed INPUT, not persisted metadata: buildRecordedFlow turns it into captureEvidence.pageKey plus one shared PageBlueprint and never writes the raw capture per step. Excluded from the comparison AND asserted separately, so the exclusion cannot hide a capture that went nowhere. Two new checks added, both cardinality-guarded (they report 'nothing was proven' when no action carried the field). MUTATION-TESTED, 3 product mutations with a rebuild in each cycle: M1 drop the recorded prerequisite -> the parity check fails (3 checks); M2 stop hashing the fingerprint -> the hashed-fingerprint check fails; M3 stamp no page evidence -> only the blueprint-consumption check fails. FIRST mutation attempt was INVALID and would have condemned the fix: the E2E launches Electron against the BUILT output ('Run after npm run build'), so mutating src/** without rebuilding showed all three as uncaught. Also removed a plaintext-leak check I had added minutes earlier: it flagged 'recorder-full-name', which is the testId selector and is supposed to persist — a check that fires on correct behaviour trains people to ignore it. RESULT: verify:recorder-e2e 58 PASS / 3 FAIL -> 63 PASS / 0 FAIL.

description: Captured with a self-describing diagnostic, not inferred. On an intermittent Workflow Builder capsule run the failure is: 'Loop indicator never appeared within 12000ms. Actual: {selectedWorkflow: verify-workflow-loop-capsule, loopEdgePresent: false, canvasNodes: 5, onLoginCard: false}'. Read that carefully - the fixture reloaded CORRECTLY: right workflow selected, not stranded on the login card, canvas rendered. What is missing is the self-loop EDGE itself. Crucially the immediately preceding waitForPersistedMaxIterations(win, 13) SUCCEEDED, so maxIterations=13 was genuinely persisted to disk before the reload. Therefore the loop edge exists in the saved workflow but intermittently does not RENDER after reopenWorkflowFixture(). If that reproduces outside the verifier it is a real user-facing defect: save a Workflow loop, reopen the workflow, and the loop is missing from the canvas while still present in the JSON. design: PREMISE FALSIFIED BY MEASUREMENT (2026-08-18). This is NOT a render bug. Soak captured a failing run with the persisted profile read from Node (not through the app bridge): the workflow file was the pristine seed, and its mtime was byte-identical to the seed mtime - the file was NEVER written after seeding. Check 13 had in fact recorded a FAIL, not a pass; '13/17 checks' counts results, not passes. ROOT CAUSE: page.waitForFunction does NOT await an async predicate. It receives a Promise, a Promise is truthy, so the wait satisfies on its first poll. Measured against real Playwright: async-always-false resolved after 105ms, sync-always-false timed out after 3010ms. Three persisted-state waits were written async (the state needs an async IPC round-trip): waitForPersistedMaxIterations in the Workflow suite and both save waits in the Flow suite. All three were inert for their whole lifetime while carrying careful comments about polling:100 vs requestAnimationFrame - correct reasoning defending a wait that never waited. The suite therefore raced past an unfinished save and reloaded, and the loop was missing on reopen for the mundane reason that it had never been saved. FIX: waitForAsyncCondition in scripts/lib/gui-verify-harness.mjs polls from Node via page.evaluate, which does await. Guard: new verify:async-wait-hygiene (16/16), mutation-tested by reverting one call site (caught it at verify-flow-loop-capsule-gui.mjs:422).
close_reason: ROOT CAUSED AND FIXED, and the original premise (a render fault) was false. Two real defects, both measured: (1) PRODUCT, user-facing data loss - JsonProfileStore.atomicWrite did tmp-write + a SINGLE rename with no retry, so routine Windows contention (antivirus, indexer, backup agent holding the destination for milliseconds) discarded the save. Captured from the app's own toast mid-flight: 'Failed to save changes. EPERM: operation not permitted, rename <...>.tmp -> <...>.json'. Affects every profile the store persists - flows, workflows, data sources, reports. Fixed by reusing app/main/atomicReplace.ts (the policy already proven for ui-settings.json under awkit-4qs): retry EPERM/EBUSY only, short linear backoff, rethrow the original errno on terminal failure. (2) INSTRUMENT - page.waitForFunction does not await an async predicate, so three persisted-state waits were inert for their whole lifetime; fixed with waitForAsyncCondition (polls from Node via evaluate, which does await) and guarded by the new verify:async-wait-hygiene. title: Recorder: init-script URL signal never reaches recordedUrls
description: CODE-READ EVIDENCE, NOT YET PROVEN BY TEST. recorderInitScript patches history.pushState/replaceState and listens to popstate+hashchange, emitting signal({kind:'url'}). But RecorderService.exposeBinding('__awtkit_recordSignal') pushes every signal into this.signals (the Smart Wait observation buffer) and returns early unless this.captureSmartWaits is true. Nothing routes kind:'url' into captureUrl()/recordedUrls. The ONLY path into recordedUrls is page.on('framenavigated') -> captureUrl. Consequences to verify: SPA route changes may produce no recorded URL at all, and with Smart Wait capture disabled the signal is discarded outright. NEXT STEP: build the focused navigation verifier (brief section 8) and measure which of goto/pushState/replaceState/hashchange/back/forward/reload actually land in recordedUrls before changing anything.
close_reason: NOT A DEFECT - disproven by measurement. verify:recorder-navigation shows pushState, replaceState and hashchange ALL reach recordedUrls: page.on('framenavigated') fires for same-document history navigations and frame.url() carries the full URL. The premise was correct (the init-script kind:'url' signal really does feed only Smart Wait) but the consequence was wrong - recordedUrls never depended on it.

The user is left with no in-app path except re-recording the step and resolving it in the Recorder ambiguity dialog.

Proposed: add a 'Use this alternative' action on each listed alternative (adopt it as primary, set resolution 'resolved' + resolvedBy 'user', clear reviewReason) and a 'Mark resolved' action for a hand-edited locator. Carry the new state through flowProfileMapping/flowStepMapping and the validation DTO. Keep the dangerous/externalCommit positional refusal absolute.

title: Ambiguous host timeout: reconcile a mutation that may or may not have been applied
description:
Carved out of awkit-9yv, which was closed on the rest of its criteria.

A request that exceeds its deadline is AMBIGUOUS: the host may have applied it, may
be about to, or may have died before touching the collection. ZvecUtilityHostManager
enforces deadlines and verify:zvec-host-lifecycle asserts the deadline VALUES are
sane (close/shutdown inside the 2s quit budget, query < open), but nothing verifies
what the system concludes about the mutation itself.

The queue must not blind-replay an ambiguous write, and must not silently drop it
either. Upserts are idempotent by deterministic id so a replay is safe; deletes are
idempotent too; deleteByEntity is idempotent. The risk is the COUNT and the
rebuildRequired decision, not the data - a timeout currently classifies through
SemanticMutationQueue retry classification, and it is untested whether that
classification is correct for an ambiguous outcome as opposed to a clean failure.

Needed:
- decide and document the policy for an ambiguous timeout (retry vs mark
  rebuild-required vs surface degraded);
- exercise it through the REAL utility host, where a timeout can actually race a
  write, not against a fake that resolves deterministically;
- add the case to verify:semantic-rebuild-live, which already kills the host
  mid-write and mid-populate and is the natural home for it.

Note for whoever picks this up: verify:zvec-host-lifecycle Timeout
notes: Policy implemented: SEMANTIC_HOST_TIMEOUT and SEMANTIC_HOST_EXITED during a dispatched write map to AMBIGUOUS_MUTATION. The queue never retries that class, abandons it, and marks rebuildRequired so authoritative source rebuild reconciles whether the host applied the operation or not. Verified through the real utility host with a 1,500-document zero-deadline write: one dispatch, one abandonment, rebuild required, no requeue. verify:semantic-store 153/153; verify:semantic-rebuild-live 24/24 with 68 assertions; semantic queue 70/70; build and script typecheck pass. Mutation disabled the mapping and produced 152/153 with three write attempts, then reverted.
close_reason: Ambiguous mutation outcomes are never blind-replayed and require authoritative rebuild, proven through the real host.

title: Semantic rebuild orchestration and generation activation
description: Keep the active generation queryable; build the candidate through the serialized rebuild path; populate only validated documents; validate schema + exact count + per-kind counts + sourceHash samples + query samples; close the candidate BEFORE pointer activation; the pointer swap is the commit point; retain one rollback generation; clear the queue and rebuildRequired flag only after successful activation; a failed candidate must never change the active pointer.

2026-07-25 (commit 67835cd, hardened by 002e684): IMPLEMENTED and verified against in-memory stores plus a generation-lifecycle stub - verify:semantic-rebuild 61/0. SemanticRebuildOrchestrator + queue watermark and ordered delta journal. Every listed requirement holds EXCEPT one, which was deliberately superseded: 'clear the queue after successful activation' is UNSAFE and is not done. A candidate is built from a snapshot, so the queue can hold mutations that postdate it; clearing on activation silently discards the user's most recent changes. Those mutations are journalled and replayed into the candidate before activation instead, and anything accepted during the replay stays pending and drains against the new generation. Delta completeness is judged against the CAPTURED entry set, not the live journal - judging against the live journal failed any rebuild that overlapped a write, so a busy index could never finish one. Journal overflow refuses activation rather than dropping entries. whenIdle() is now bounded by wall-clock as well as iterations (an iteration bound does not bound time; a wedged rebuild would have held shutdown open forever). NOT DONE: the orchestrator is not bound to a real generation root - rebuildGeneration/openCandidate/retarget still need wiring to rebuildIntoNewGeneration and a real runtime root, and whenIdle() has no production shutdown caller. title: Zvec host: add scan/count/cursor + typed filters to remove the 100-document ceiling
description: The utility host protocol has no scan or cursor operation. Its query is top-K capped at 100 and the raw host returns hit counts plus ten ids, not documents. Consequently ZvecSemanticStore cannot implement deleteByEntity, stats, clear or an exact totalMatched correctly, and currently declares capabilities.entityOperations=false and throws UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION for them (safer than silently truncating). Search also over-fetches the global top 100 then applies AWKIT filters after ranking, so a filtered match ranked outside the unfiltered top 100 is never returned and totalMatched is not the true filtered total. Needs: typed host operations (scan with cursor/page, exact count, deleteByEntity, clearCollection, query with typed filters applied INSIDE the trusted adapter/host, never a raw filter expression crossing SemanticStore). Proofs required: clear 1500 docs leaves zero; delete an entity with >100 docs leaves zero; a filtered match beyond the unfiltered top 100 is found; totalMatched exact.
notes: RESOLVED in code on main (f4f6a37, 5f6250a). Host protocol v2 adds typed scan/count/deleteByFilter; ZvecSemanticStore.capabilities.entityOperations is now true. All four required proofs hold against the REAL @zvec/zvec binding via verify:semantic-zvec-filter (63/0): clear removes all 1501 docs; an entity with 130 docs (>100) deletes completely; a filtered match ranked last of 1501 is found at topk=10 while the unfiltered top-10 excludes it (negative-controlled); totalMatched is exact via a count-only second pass. The original premise was WRONG: the 100-doc ceiling was AWKIT's own Math.min(topK,100) in the host, not a vendor limit, and deleteByFilterSync existed all along. Filters cross IPC as typed clauses only; the host builds the expression from an allowlist (duplicated deliberately, drift-checked). Value rule is a REFUSAL not an escaper - measured: escaping only quotes throws on backslash values, escaping both silently matches NOTHING. RESIDUAL GAP: the host's own code path (its duplicated builder, two-pass query, post-delete re-scan) is asserted by source-drift checks, not executed through a real utilityProcess. That execution proof is awkit-9yv.
close_reason: Implemented on main (f4f6a37, 5f6250a); all four required proofs verified against the real binding. Remaining end-to-end proof through a real utilityProcess is tracked by awkit-9yv, which already specifies exactly that.

title: Make offline packaging inputs versioned and verifiable
description:
Packaged artifacts are NOT reproducible from source control, and a clean checkout can produce a
valid-LOOKING but unusable application.

Found while regenerating artifacts from 61f6099 (see C:\Users\moham\awkit-build-evidence\61f6099\provenance.md).

Problems:
1. `vendor/` is fully gitignored (0 files tracked). `resources/browsers/` and
   `resources/oracle-jdbc/` are gitignored too -- only 27 of 339 `resources/` files are tracked.
   electron-builder.json copies BOTH trees wholesale as `extraResources`.
   => A pristine checkout builds a ~830 MB-lighter artifact with NO bundled Chromium. It packages
      and launches, but cannot automate anything. Nothing fails loudly.
2. `scripts/prepare-offline-deps.ps1:17` runs a bare, unqualified `npx playwright install chromium`
   and copies whatever lands in the machine's ms-playwright cache. No version is requested, pinned,
   or verified before the copy.
3. CLEAN_MACHINE_VALIDATION_RUNBOOK.md §2 pins the final artifact SHA-256 but NOT the browser
   payload that materially determines the artifact's behaviour and most of its bytes.
   => The hash pins roughly half the input.
4. `resources/dependency-manifest.json`.`application.builtAt` records MANIFEST REGENERATION time,
   not the age of the bundled browser payload. Observed concretely: a 2026-07-22 build wrote
   builtAt=2026-07-22 while shipping the Chromium payload dated 2026-07-10. A reader would date the
   payload 12 days later than it is. (Split out as its own P2 bead -- see the metadata-naming bead.)
acceptance_criteria:
1. Packaging FAILS FAST, before the build, when required offline resources are missing or
   incomplete -- never produces a hollow artifact.
2. Expected Chromium and Playwright versions are explicit and declared in-repo.
3. The installed browser payload is verified by version AND hash before it is copied into
   vendor/ / resources/browsers/.
4. No bare, floating browser installation. `npx playwright install chromium` is replaced by a
   version-qualified, verified acquisition step.
5. Artifact provenance records, together: source commit, browser version, browser-payload
   hash + source date, Playwright version, Electron version, final artifact hash.
6. A clean checkout + an approved offline payload produces a COMPLETE package with no network
   access.
7. Reproducibility is validated by SEMANTIC PAYLOAD EQUIVALENCE, not whole-artifact hash equality:
   compare decompressed payload paths, sizes, and per-entry CRCs between the two artifacts,
   EXCLUDING known volatile generated metadata (currently
   `resources\resources\dependency-manifest.json` and its `vendor\` copy). Any other differing
   entry is real drift and must be investigated.
8. Whole-installer SHA-256 equality is NOT expected while build-time timestamps are embedded.
   `scripts/package-per-user-installer.ps1` regenerates `resources/dependency-manifest.json` (fresh
   `builtAt`) on every run and packages it, so two builds from byte-identical inputs yield
   different installer hashes. Final artifact SHA-256 is still recorded for runbook pinning and
   integrity verification -- it identifies the SPECIFIC ACCEPTED BUILD and must not be presented as
   proof of reproducible compilation. See awkit-c0c for the metadata split that would reduce this.
notes:
P1 because the failure mode is silent: a clean checkout yields a package that installs and launches but cannot drive a browser. Evidence + logs: C:\Users\moham\awkit-build-evidence\61f6099\. Keep SEPARATE from the clean-machine acceptance gate and from the 61f6099 artifact regeneration -- this is a repository-quality defect, not a release blocker for the current gate.
2026-07-28 Codex: implemented the authorized fail-loud half only. Both portable and NSIS packaging wrappers now invoke validate-offline-bundle.ps1 -PackagingInputsOnly before npm run build. The preflight names the exact resources/browsers/chromium/chrome.exe path and refuses missing or zero-byte inputs. Positive gate passed on the current payload; missing-file and empty-file mutations both failed loudly. Full validate:offline and strict validation pass. Bead remains OPEN because acceptance items 2-8 and the Chromium vendoring/reproducibility strategy require the owner decision explicitly reserved by docs/ai/tasks/DASHBOARD_BACKLOG_PROGRAM.md.
close_reason: Closed with exact Playwright/CfT pins and archive/tree/executable hashes, Ed25519-signed manifest plus startup verification, fail-fast packaging gates, artifact provenance, tamper tests, deterministic Oracle bridge, and clean-clone offline packaging. Two independent portable artifacts matched across 571 decompressed entries after excluding the generated signed manifest metadata and normalizing only Zvec builtAt.

title: Artifact profile screenshotOnFailure is computed but never read
description:
Configuration-contract defect: the Flow Designer and the resolved artifact profile imply one
behaviour while the runtime follows a different switch.

`resolveArtifactSettings()` returns `screenshotOnFailure` for all four profiles
(src/runner/artifacts/ArtifactProfile.ts:22-38), but NOTHING READS IT. The real gate is
`step.onFailure?.screenshot ?? true` (src/runner/FlowExecutor.ts:446).

Result: the `production` artifact profile does not actually control failure screenshots, and
`AWKIT_ARTIFACT_PROFILE=production` does not lean out failure-screenshot capture as documented.
Config that lies.
acceptance_criteria:
1. An explicit precedence contract is implemented and documented:

     explicit per-step override    (step.onFailure.screenshot, when present)
       -> artifact profile default (resolveArtifactSettings().screenshotOnFailure)
         -> safe system default    (capture)

   Concretely: the `?? true` fallback becomes `?? resolvedArtifactSettings.screenshotOnFailure`.
2. Flows that EXPLICITLY disable failure screenshots continue to disable them. The profile governs
   only steps with NO explicit override.
3. AWKIT_ARTIFACT_PROFILE=production demonstrably suppresses failure screenshots for steps with no
   explicit override; balanced/debug/full still capture.
4. Regression test proves the old always-capture behaviour is gone for the profile-governed case
   AND that the explicit opt-out still wins.
5. Either the field is wired (preferred) or removed -- no third state where it exists unread.
notes: Spec: docs/SRS_BROWSER_AUTOMATION_OBSERVABILITY.md FR-A4 change-dependency (Tranche 0). Prerequisite for detail-tiered observability: do not ship a second tier on top of a tier that already lies about one of its three fields. Keep SEPARATE from the evidence-ordering bead (awkit-oyc) despite adjacent code.

title: Failure evidence is captured after the retry loop, not at the failing attempt
description:
The failure screenshot is taken in `FlowExecutor.runStepWithRetries` AFTER the whole retry loop
finishes (src/runner/FlowExecutor.ts:446-448), guarded by `step.onFailure?.screenshot ?? true`.

Consequences:
- Retries that navigate, refresh, dismiss a dialog, or re-render DESTROY the broken state before it
  is photographed. The captured image is not the failure.
- Intermediate failed attempts get no evidence at all.

`StepExecutor.execute`'s catch block (src/runner/StepExecutor.ts:287-307) already holds the correct
per-attempt scope and already saves the trace chunk there for exactly this reason -- evidence
capture belongs alongside it.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Evidence is captured INSIDE the failing attempt's scope, before any retry, recovery, or
   navigation can alter page state.
2. Each retry attempt produces its own evidence set; attempt n's evidence is never overwritten by
   attempt n+1.
3. Each failed attempt preserves all four independently:
     - original exception  (always primary; never replaced)
     - attempt-specific evidence  (screenshot, DOM, a11y, console tail, network state)
     - trace chunk  (existing TraceService.endStep behaviour)
     - retry decision  (the RetryPolicy verdict + reason; runtime_node_attempts.retryDecision)
4. Evidence-capture failure is APPENDED as a secondary diagnostic and never replaces, masks, or
   reorders the original automation error. A dead page still reports the step's real failure.
5. Evidence filenames encode runId, flowId, stepId, pageId, attemptId, timestamp.
6. Capture is bounded -- a hung page must not block the failure path indefinitely.
7. `StepExecutionResult.screenshotPath` STILL populated with the last capture (FlowExecutor.ts:446
   checks `!lastResult.screenshotPath` and the reports UI reads it). New per-attempt refs are
   additive.
8. Captures routed through the existing OperationLimiters (`limitOp`) so concurrent runs do not
   stampede on screenshots.
notes: Spec: docs/SRS_BROWSER_AUTOMATION_OBSERVABILITY.md FR-B2 (Tranche 1). Highest diagnostic value per unit of risk; independent of CDP. Preserve the step.onFailure.screenshot opt-out -- saved flows rely on it. Keep as a SEPARATE bead from the artifact-profile precedence fix (awkit-5yx) even though the code is adjacent: different failure mode, different acceptance criteria, different rollback boundary.
close_reason: Reconciled the shipped FR-B2 fix from 269cd70/b4d2974: FlowExecutor captures every failing attempt before RetryPolicy.decide, accumulates evidence without replacing the automation error, and preserves screenshotPath. Extended verify:failure-evidence with an explicit capture-before-decision timeline sentinel: 35/35; moving decide ahead of capture produced 34/35 and was reverted. Real Chromium evidence output remains 17/17.

title: Popup registration is non-deterministic: one Page registered under two aliases
description:
A single popup Page is registered under TWO aliases by two independent call sites.

- `PlaywrightRunner.runFlowWithChildren` installs a context-level `page` handler that assigns
  `popup-${++runnerPopupCounter}` (src/runner/PlaywrightRunner.ts:471-479) -- a POSITIONAL key.
- The click path separately registers the recorded alias via
  `registerPopupPage(expectation.popupAlias, popupPage)` (src/runner/StepExecutor.ts:1255).

Both fire for the same popup. Consequences: the same Page is reachable under two keys, and the
counter-derived key depends on arrival order, so multi-window flows replay non-deterministically
when popups open in a different order than at record time.

NOTE: you cannot simply delete one path. The runner handler is the ONLY registration for
script-/timer-/redirect-opened popups; the click path is the ONLY one that applies the RECORDED
alias. The fix must reconcile them into one owner in a single change.
acceptance_criteria:
1. ONE registration mechanism owns the page registry; registration is not performed from two
   independent call sites.
2. A popup with a recorded `popupExpectation.popupAlias` is registered under THAT alias only.
3. A popup with no recorded expectation gets ONE deterministic synthetic alias derived from
   identity-bearing attributes (opener step id + target URL origin), never from arrival order.
4. INVARIANT: the same `Page` object is never reachable under more than one alias. A verifier
   asserts registry values are distinct.
5. Two popups opening in reversed order across runs resolve to the same aliases in both runs.
6. A closed-and-reopened popup does not inherit the previous page's alias.
7. Legacy recorded aliases (`popup-1`, `popup-2`, ...) still resolve unchanged.
8. Mock-site scenarios added for reversed-popup-order AND script-opened-popup (AGENTS.md requires
   mock-site coverage for runner/recorder features); `verify:recorder` + `verify:runner` green.

title: Designer round trip silently drops a bare FlowStep.value (condition expressions)
description:
DATA LOSS. fromFlowStep (app/renderer/components/workflow/flowStepMapping.ts) derives the node's value as:

    step.url ?? valueSource?.value ?? valueSource?.key ?? valueSource?.envKey ?? valueSource?.path ?? valueSource?.outputKey ?? ""

It NEVER reads step.value. So a FlowStep carrying only `value` (no `valueSource`, and not a goto) resolves to "" on load, and toFlowStep then emits `value: data.value || undefined` -> undefined. The value is destroyed by one designer open+save, with no error shown.

REACHABLE ON SHIPPED DATA: resources/test-fixtures/mock-site/flows/mock-conditional-flow.json stores its condition node with a `value` expression and no valueSource. Confirmed against the real converters:

    BEFORE  value = "<runtimeInputs.path expression>"   valueSource = undefined
    AFTER   value = undefined                           valueSource = undefined
    RESULT: condition expression LOST

Impact: opening such a flow in the Flow Designer and saving turns a working conditional into an empty one. A scan of resources/** found 69 steps with 1 currently affected. Externally authored or imported flows can hit this more broadly, since FlowStep.value is an independent optional field in the schema.

Found by scripts/verify-flow-step-mapping.mts during the Serialization Round-Trip Hardening phase. NOT introduced by the extraction: the moved functions are byte-identical to the originals (proven by diff). Pre-existing defect.

Current behavior is PINNED by two checks in that verifier under the "KNOWN DEFECT" section. When this is fixed, those two checks must be inverted.

Likely fix: either have fromFlowStep fall back to step.value when there is no url and no valueSource, OR require producers to always emit a static valueSource alongside value. Both are runtime behavior changes, so both were deliberately excluded from the hardening phase. Needs a decision on which side owns the invariant.
notes: FIXED (uncommitted, 2026-07-22) on feature/recorder-protected-login-and-async-awareness. Chose the designer-boundary fix: fromFlowStep reads step.value and marks a designer-only valueSourceType:'none' sentinel; createValueSource returns undefined for it so toFlowStep re-emits value alone WITHOUT fabricating a static valueSource. Inverted the 2 pinned KNOWN-DEFECT checks + added string/numeric/boolean/json/empty coverage. Same-class drops of generated(generator)+secret(secretName) found in the §8 pass and also fixed. verify:flow-step-mapping 94/0, tsc 0. Close on commit.

title: RT-14: value and valueSource flattened through one designer string, corrupting typed sources
description:
fromFlowStep collapses FlowStep.value and FlowStep.valueSource into a single data.value via: step.url ?? valueSource?.value ?? valueSource?.key ?? valueSource?.envKey ?? valueSource?.path ?? valueSource?.outputKey ?? "". createValueSource then rebuilds a typed source from that one string.

Most damaging round-trip finding. On a goto, step.url is FIRST in the chain and shadows the source entirely: {type:env, envKey:AWKIT_LAB_ENV_ALPHA} returns as {type:env, envKey:http://127.0.0.1:4321/form.html}, and {type:generated, generator:randomEmail} returns with a generator value outside its own union (a structurally invalid document). For other types, FlowStep.value is overwritten with the SOURCE KEY, destroying the literal fallback the runner would use. Sources whose discriminating field is not in the chain (secret, dynamic) collapse to empty and are dropped - this is also the mechanism behind RT-02.

Owner: app/renderer/components/workflow/flowProfileMapping.ts (fromFlowStep + createValueSource).
Fix: model the value source structurally in FlowDesignerNodeData instead of flattening. Immediate containment: remove step.url from the head of the recovery chain - it is the only entry that can silently overwrite an unrelated source field.
Reproduce: npx tsx scripts/verify-random-roundtrip.mts (fixed seed awkit-roundtrip-baseline-001). Full diff, minimal failing definition and both original/reloaded definitions are in reports/random-tests/roundtrip-defects.json.
close_reason: Fixed. valueSourceOriginal preserves the loaded source verbatim; createValueSource reconstructs only the two panel-authorable kinds (static/dynamic) and passes the rest through; data.value is the literal only; toFlowStep no longer persists url:''. title: verify:branding sanity check demands removing the deliberate license-issuer boundary
description: Full-suite run 2026-08-18: verify:branding 46/47. Failing check (scripts/verify-branding.mts:168): 'SuperUser holds every permission (sanity)' — ALL_PERMISSIONS.every(p => BUILTIN_ROLES.SuperUser.permissions.includes(p)). SuperUser is missing exactly page.licenseIssuer and license.issue (ALL=42, SuperUser=40). THIS IS NOT A PRODUCT DEFECT AND MUST NOT BE 'FIXED' IN THE PRODUCT. src/security/authz/Permissions.ts builds SUPER_USER_PERMISSIONS as ALL_PERMISSIONS minus ISSUER_PERMISSIONS, with the documented reason: 'Issuer is deliberately narrow and exclusive... so a direct grant or the Super User's broad permission set can never become a signing-key boundary bypass.' Granting SuperUser those permissions would weaken a signing-key boundary. The assertion predates that boundary. ACTION: re-express it, as awkit-gc0g did — assert that SuperUser holds every permission EXCEPT the issuer set, AND assert the issuer set is held by no built-in role, so the boundary itself becomes the thing under test instead of being contradicted.
close_reason: FIXED by re-expressing the assertion. NO product change — and that mattered here more than usual, because satisfying the check as written would have required GRANTING SuperUser the license-issuer permissions, i.e. removing a security boundary to make a test green. CONFIRMED FROM SOURCE at three layers, not from memory: (1) Permissions.ts builds SUPER_USER_PERMISSIONS as ALL_PERMISSIONS minus ISSUER_PERMISSIONS with the documented reason 'so a direct grant or the Super Users broad permission set can never become a signing-key boundary bypass'; (2) the Issuer built-in role holds exactly those two; (3) UserAdminService rejects an Issuer who also holds any other role (ISSUER_ROLE_EXCLUSIVE) and the licenseIssuer route requires that exact role. CORRECTION TO THIS BEADS OWN INSTRUCTION: it proposed asserting the issuer set is held by NO built-in role. That would have been wrong — the Issuer role holds them by design. Checked before writing, so it did not ship. THE SANITY INTENT IS KEPT, NOT DROPPED. One assertion became three: SuperUser holds every permission except the issuer pair; the ONLY permissions withheld from SuperUser are that pair (an exact set difference, so a newly withheld permission still fails); and the Issuer role holds exactly that pair, so neither permission is orphaned nor bundled with unrelated power. The two names are restated in the verifier rather than imported (ISSUER_PERMISSIONS is not exported), so widening the boundary in the product surfaces as a failure needing review instead of being mirrored silently. MUTATION-TESTED, 3 mutations, each caught by its intended check: M1 grant SuperUser the issuer permissions — the exact change the OLD assertion demanded — now FAILS the boundary check (48/49); M2 widen ISSUER_PERMISSIONS to withhold a third permission fails all three (46/49); M3 empty the Issuer role fails only the orphan check (48/49). So the verifier has flipped from requiring a security regression to forbidding one. RESULTS: verify:branding 46/47 -> 49/49; adjacent gates unaffected — verify:licensing 183/183, verify:authz 92/92, verify:recorder-authz 58/58.

title: verify:recorder-competitive drop-target check encodes the pre-awkit-65g positional expectation

title: Capsule suites never assert the absence of a save-error toast
description: Found while root-causing awkit-a53k. The Workflow capsule suite clicked Save, the app raised a visible 'Failed to save changes. EPERM ...' toast, and every downstream check carried on as though the save had succeeded. The vacuous async wait was the proximate cause, but no check asserted the absence of an error toast either, so any FUTURE save failure with a different cause would again surface as a confusing downstream timeout rather than naming itself. Also note the toast auto-dismisses, so an assertion that reads after a long wait finds nothing - it must sample during the wait (see waitForPersistedMaxIterations in scripts/lib/verify-workflow-loop-capsule-gui.mjs, which now keeps the last toast it sees). ACTION: after every Save click in both capsule suites, assert no .app-toast with tone error is present, and fail with its text if one is.
close_reason: FIXED. All four Save clicks across the two capsule suites (2 Flow, 2 Workflow) are immediately followed by a persist wait, so one shared helper covers every save: waitForPersistedState in scripts/lib/gui-verify-harness.mjs polls the persisted state and reads .app-toast-error on every poll, failing IMMEDIATELY with the app's own message rather than waiting out the timeout. Two design points the bead called for: (a) the toast auto-dismisses, so it is sampled during the wait, never read afterwards - reading afterwards captured only the status bar ('Save failed', the fact without the cause); (b) only toasts appearing AFTER the wait starts are fatal, since a stale toast from an earlier step would otherwise abort a perfectly healthy save. The predicate is also read BEFORE the toast, so a save landing in the same tick as an unrelated error is reported as the success it is. Consolidation: waitForAsyncCondition had no callers left once all three sites moved to waitForPersistedState, so it was removed rather than left as an exported helper nothing calls; verify:async-wait-hygiene now points at the surviving construction. EVIDENCE: verify:async-wait-hygiene 16 -> 22 checks, the six new ones proving the helper behaviourally against a stand-in page whose evaluate awaits (fails on a fresh error toast, fails fast at 2ms not the timeout, carries the EPERM text, ignores a stale toast, still times out when nothing is wrong, and reports the described state). Mutation-tested: disabling the guard fails exactly those three checks and reproduces the original symptom - 'never became true within 5000ms' after 5004ms. verify:flow-designer exit 0 (capsule 16/16, broad 112, retired 0, unexpected 0); verify:workflow-builder exit 0 (capsule 17/17, broad 58, retired 0, unexpected 0).

title: Recorder: action-caused navigation has no regression test (M1 mutation survives)
description: awkit-76x added a goto step for INDEPENDENT navigation, keyed on whether a recorded action occurred on the page since its last navigation (RecorderService.captureUrl). title: Recorder: independent mid-recording navigation has no representation in the replayable flow
description: MEASURED via verify:recorder-navigation. buildRecordedFlow(name, actions, blueprints) never sees recordedUrls, and 'goto' is pushed as an action exactly ONCE - at recording start, for the initial target URL. So a recorded flow contains exactly one navigation step. Action-caused navigation replays implicitly through Playwright auto-waiting, which matches brief section 9's stated preference for navigation metadata on the triggering action over redundant Navigate steps. The gap is section 9's THIRD case: independent navigation during recording (user types a URL, uses the back button, an external redirect lands elsewhere) has no representation at all, so replay diverges silently from what was recorded. Decide deliberately whether that needs an explicit navigation step or is out of scope; do not add a Navigate step after every URL change, which section 9 explicitly warns against.
close_reason: captureUrl now emits a goto for independent navigation, keyed on whether a recorded action occurred on the page since its last navigation. verify:recorder-navigation 20/20; recorder suites green. The action-caused half remains unproven - see awkit-r4d.

title: Recorder: emitUrl strips hash and query, so hash/query-only navigation is indistinguishable
description: CODE-READ EVIDENCE, NOT YET PROVEN BY TEST. recorderInitScript emitUrl() emits 'location.origin + location.pathname', discarding both the hash and the query string, and sets __awtkitLastObservedUrl to the same truncated value. A hashchange (#a -> #b) or a query-only SPA route change (?page=1 -> ?page=2) therefore emits a URL identical to the previous one. Combined with upsertUrl dedup in RecorderService.captureUrl, such a transition is likely recorded as nothing. Note captureUrl separately applies maskUrl for sensitive query values - any fix must preserve that masking rather than emitting raw query strings.
close_reason: NOT A DEFECT - disproven by measurement. emitUrl() really does emit origin+pathname, but recordedUrls is fed by frame.url() via framenavigated, not by emitUrl. Measured: pushState records /login?spa=1 (query preserved), hashchange records /login?spa=2#sec2 (hash preserved), and a hash-only move stays distinguishable from its base URL. emitUrl's truncation affects only Smart Wait attribution, where it may well be intentional.

title: Gitignored paths are invisible to the lease audit, including owned and protected ones
description: git status never reports ignored files, so the Bash audit cannot see writes to them. Enumerating all ignored files is not an option (node_modules). Two concrete defects found: build/** is release-owned and implies packaging_change but is fully gitignored with zero tracked files, so a lease over it protects nothing observable; and resources/** is PROTECTED (Risk 3, offline boundary) while resources/browsers/ and resources/oracle-jdbc/ are gitignored subtrees. Also consequential and invisible: .env*, .claude/settings.local.json, storage-state.json, auth-state.json, session-profiles.json - secrets, permissions and captured auth. Fix with a bounded WATCHED_IGNORED_PATHS fingerprinted by mtime/size at lease grant, plus a verifier check that no protected path is git-invisible and unwatched. Out of scope by design: node_modules, out, dist - derived artifacts.
close_reason: WATCHED_IGNORED_PATHS fingerprints the consequential gitignored paths (secrets, local permissions, captured auth, build/, and the ignored subtrees of protected resources/). Found and fixed two registry defects: build/** owned but zero tracked files, resources/** protected with invisible interiors. verify:agent-routing 298/298, mutation 7/7 (40/40 all suites).

title: No-lease gap: unclaimed edits to Risk 3 paths are unrestricted
description: The lease guard allows every edit when no lease is held, because failing closed would block every task that does not use a contract. That is right for ordinary work and wrong for the paths the repo already treats as critical. Fix: derive PROTECTED_PATHS from PATH_DOMAINS entries whose impliesFlags intersect RISK_3_FLAGS (licensing, auth, secrets, security, resources/offline boundary) and require an active lease for those specifically. Ordinary paths stay unrestricted with no lease; protected paths fail closed. Derived rather than hand-listed so it stays correct as flags evolve. The Bash audit gets the symmetric rule: with no lease it compares protected paths against HEAD.
close_reason: PROTECTED_PATHS derived from RISK_3_FLAGS: licensing, auth, secrets, security, resources refuse an unclaimed write; ordinary paths stay unrestricted. Symmetric rule in the Bash audit. decideWrite() extracted so the guard's judgement is testable. verify:agent-routing 277/277, mutation 5/5 (33/33 all suites).

title: Bash writes bypass the write-lease guard entirely
description: The PreToolUse guard matches Edit|Write|NotebookEdit, so a shell redirect, sed -i, mv, or git checkout never reaches it. Parsing shell to guess write intent is unreliable in both directions and is explicitly rejected. Fix by observing actual filesystem state instead: a PostToolUse hook on Bash compares git status against the lease scope plus the dirty set recorded at grant time, records any out-of-lease modification onto the lease, and blocks completion until resolved. Detection rather than prevention - the write has already happened - but immediate and attributable instead of invisible. Costs ~100ms per Bash call only while a lease is held; with no lease it exits before touching git. Known residual: gitignored paths are invisible to git status.
close_reason: PostToolUse audit on Bash observes git status rather than parsing shell; out-of-lease writes are named, recorded on the lease, and block completion. Detection not prevention. verify:agent-routing 256/256, mutation-tested 6/6 (28/28 across all suites).

title: package.json lease friction: a one-line script addition requires a release lease handoff
description: package.json is release-owned because it carries the dependency graph, so adding an npm script forces a full lease handoff. The path map is file-granular but the risk in package.json is concentrated in specific KEYS. Fix: allow shared write access for the scripts field only, and enforce the rest with a derived, content-aware check that compares HEAD's package.json against the working tree - relax the edit-time gate that cannot see content, enforce with the derived check that can. Default-guarded: any field other than the explicitly shared ones is release-owned, so a new top-level key is guarded automatically.
close_reason: package.json is now a shared write path for the scripts field only. Edit-time gate relaxed (it cannot see content); enforcement moved to deriveGuardedFieldChanges(), which reports any non-shared field change as a scope escape. Default-guarded. verify:agent-routing 242/242, mutation-tested 6/6. Demonstrated live: a script added under a QA lease, a dependency edit under the same lease reported as an escape.

title: Router: writerSequence lists agents that own none of the task's paths

Misleading, and validate-contract.mjs derives touchesProductCode from writerSequence.length, so any naive narrowing would fail OPEN and stop requiring a writer. Fix: restrict the sequence to activated writers that own at least one expected path, fall back to all activated writers when that is empty or no paths are declared, and reclassify the dropped writer-mode agents as consultants.

title: Blueprint page-key never matches framed targets; documentFingerprint variant-gate unused
description: Two runtime defects in the blueprint recovery feature. (1) Frame page-key mismatch: at capture (src/recorder/buildRecordedFlow.ts ~line 72) computePageKey uses the frame's captured url/title; at runtime (src/runner/LocatorFactory.ts ~line 425) it uses this.page.url()/this.page.title() = the TOP page. So any iframe target computes a different pageKey at replay and the blueprint is never found — blueprint recovery is effectively non-functional for frames/shadow targets the plan lists as scenarios. frameKey is also just the literal string 'frame' (not a real chain digest) and frameChainDigest/shadowChainDigest are never populated in the assembled ElementBlueprint. (2) documentFingerprint (page-variant detection) is captured and stored but NEVER checked at runtime before trusting a blueprint. Both degrade safely (fall through), so no crash — but the frame scenarios do not work. Minor cleanup in same area: ElementBlueprint.ancestry is stored raw/unhashed while the plan requires hashed identity fields.

title: Issuer private key has no synced-folder custody check (SPECTER_ISSUER_KEY)
description:
Found during TAKEOFF review on 2026-08-02, after awkit-0tn (issuer console) landed in 9f391c9.

app/main/licensing/issuerRuntime.ts:16-23 resolves the issuer signing key to
  getRuntimeDataRoot()/issuer-keys/key1.ed25519.pkcs8.b64
overridable by the SPECTER_ISSUER_KEY environment variable. Neither path is checked for cloud-sync custody.

The DEFAULT is fine: getRuntimeDataRoot() is %LOCALAPPDATA%/SpecterStudio, which is not synced. The gap is the override. An operator can point SPECTER_ISSUER_KEY at a path inside OneDrive/Dropbox/Google Drive/iCloud/Box and the issuer console will happily sign customer licenses with a key that is being continuously copied to a cloud account - the exact custody problem awkit-2l1 exists to end, one product surface over, and with a broader blast radius: this key signs licences for other machines, not just our own dependency manifest.

Precedent and the reason this is not a one-line fix: scripts/lib/release-key-custody.mjs already implements the rule (whole-path-segment detection for seven providers plus the sync clients' own env vars, fail-closed assertKeyCustody, redactPath so no account name reaches a log, and an exact-'1' override). It cannot simply be imported here - it is a build-time .mjs under scripts/, while the issuer runs inside the bundled Electron main process. The rule needs lifting into shared app code (src/) that both the packaging script and the main process can consume, without duplicating the detection table.

Suggested shape:
  1. Move the detection + custody assertion into src/ (e.g. src/security/keyCustody.ts) with no Node-only assumptions beyond node:path.
  2. Have scripts/lib/release-key-custody.mjs delegate to it, so there is one detection table and the existing verify:release-key-custody keeps covering it.
  3. Call assertKeyCustody in LicenseIssuerService before the key is read, so issuance fails closed with the same actionable, redacted message.
  4. Extend verify:licensing (or verify:release-key-custody) with an issuer case, and mutation-test that removing the call re-admits a synced key path.

Do NOT read, move, copy or rotate any issuer key while doing this - same standing rule as awkit-2l1. The work is path reasoning only; no key material is needed to build or test it.

Related: awkit-2l1 (release-manifest key custody, owner action still pending).

The custody rule now covers the issuer key too. New src/security/keyCustody.ts is the canonical statement (whole-path-segment detection for seven providers plus the sync clients' own env vars, evaluateKeyCustody failing closed, redactKeyPath, exact-'1' override reusing AWKIT_ALLOW_SYNCED_SIGNING_KEY). LicenseIssuerService.loadSigningKey evaluates it BEFORE readFile and throws the new ISSUER_KEY_UNSAFE_LOCATION reason - a key we must not use is not one we should open. Because loadSigningKey is the single funnel, readiness() reports it as well as issue(). The Issuer page gives a specific, actionable message instead of a fallback.

Two implementations remain, deliberately and provably in sync: the packaging signer runs under plain node and cannot import TypeScript, and allowJs is false so the app cannot import the .mjs. verify:release-key-custody moved from .mjs to .mts (with a .d.mts for the script-side module) so it imports BOTH and drives ONE fixture table through them, asserting identical verdicts, identical redaction, the same provider list and the same override variable. title: Recorder verifier harness installs the init script after page load, not at document start
description:
Found while starting awkit-hmt on 2026-08-02.

Production injects the recorder with context.addInitScript (RecorderService.ts:691, and :615 for popups), so it installs at DOCUMENT START, before page scripts. scripts/verify-recorder-hover.mts installs it with page.evaluate AFTER page.goto, so 191 checks all exercise an install order the product never uses. The same pattern is likely in the other recorder verifiers.

Measured differences (probes run 2026-08-02, both orders, same fixtures):
- ORDINARY CLICKS ARE UNAFFECTED. A 282-element page and a synthetic 1807-element page both recorded clean clicks under either order, with controls placed before AND after the bulk of the document. The per-root descendant cap (INSERTION_NODES_PER_BATCH=64) keeps the initial parse from exhausting INSERTION_RECORD_CAP, so there is no parse-time saturation and no spurious needs-review. This was checked specifically because the fail-closed guard added in db0babd could have regressed every recording on a large page. It does not.
- Switching the harness to addInitScript gives 187/191: only section [23] (fail-closed saturation) fails.

Why [23] fails under the production order, and the real finding: at document start the baseline scan runs on an empty DOM, so EVERY element is later recorded as an insertion with a null witness. nearestInsertion() walks up to 8 ancestors and finds one of those parse-time records, returns it, and the resolver exits at 'no witness' — so the saturation branch is never reached. The fail-closed guard is therefore largely INERT under the production install order. Positives are unaffected because the target's own record is checked at depth 0 before any ancestor.

Two things to decide:
1. Switch the recorder verifiers to context.addInitScript so they test the shipped install order. Expect to rework section [23].
2. Either make the saturation guard distinguish 'the target itself has no record' from 'an ancestor has a witness-less parse record', or drop it and stop claiming fail-closed behaviour that does not fire in production.

Also relevant to any future work that needs page-registered listener evidence (e.g. wrapping addEventListener to detect hover listeners): that signal only exists when the recorder installs first, so it cannot be tested at all until the harness is fixed.
close_reason: Both halves fixed. PRODUCT: the at-rest baseline ran the instant the script executed, which under context.addInitScript is document start, before the page markup is parsed - so absentAtBaseline was true for the whole page, the initial parse was recorded as insertions with null witnesses (burning up to INSERTION_RECORD_CAP records at load), and nearestInsertion found one of those on an ancestor of nearly any target, making the fail-closed saturation guard unreachable. startObservation now runs on DOMContentLoaded (or immediately if already parsed), so 'at rest' means the loaded page under either install order. Positives were never affected (a target's own record is checked before any ancestor), which is why three tasks of green runs never showed it. HARNESS: verify-recorder-hover and verify-recorder-ambiguity now install via context.addInitScript like the product (verify-recorder-locator already did), and a new source guard asserts across every recorder verifier that none injects with page.evaluate and all use addInitScript, cardinality-checked first. Mutation-proven both ways: undoing the deferral fails the saturation section (4 checks); reverting one verifier to post-load injection fails the source guard by name. verify:recorder-hover 214/214 under the production order; recorder 171/171, ambiguity 62/62, recorder-draft 50/50, recorder-redaction 15 PASS, REC-018 61 PASS, Recorder GUI 166 PASS, runner 89/89, mock-site 110/110 all green.

title: Flow Designer: hover nodes render as Start because the catalog lookup silently falls back to entry zero
description:
getFlowNodeCatalogItem (app/renderer/components/workflow/flowNodeCatalog.ts:79-81) is:

  return flowNodeCatalog.find((item) => item.type === type) ?? flowNodeCatalog[0];

flowNodeCatalog[0] is the 'start' entry {label: 'Start', description: 'Flow entry point', icon: Play}. 'hover' is registered in flowNodeRegistry.ts:64 (category interaction, executable) but has NO catalog entry, so every hover step on the canvas renders as a Start node with the Play icon and the text 'Flow entry point'. Confirmed by diffing the two files: of the real node types, hover is the ONLY one missing from the catalog.

Cosmetic only - execution reads the registry, not the catalog - but a hover step that looks like a flow entry point is actively misleading when reading a canvas, and it shipped silently because nothing checks registry/catalog parity. Introduced when Increment 5 (awkit-aui.5) added hover capture and registered the type without a catalog entry.

Same silent-degradation shape as the icon() ?? ICON_NODES.circle fallback: a lookup keyed by a developer-supplied literal that renders something PLAUSIBLE for an unknown key instead of failing.

Fix: (1) add a proper hover catalog entry with its own icon, label and description; (2) add a registry<->catalog parity verifier so a future node type cannot repeat this - it must assert both directions and carry a cardinality guard so it cannot pass over an empty scan; (3) replace the ?? flowNodeCatalog[0] fallback with an explicit Unknown-step rendering or a development assertion. An unknown node type must never impersonate a valid Start node.

title: Undo migration is offered for records that cannot be undone
description:
Regression introduced by my own fa87fc8, found by clean-machine runbook 8.7 on 2026-07-30 (seventh sitting, Pass D).

fa87fc8 made FlowChartDesigner re-read validation:migrations on load and re-offer the newest not-yet-undone migration, so undo survives a restart. The filter is only !record.undoneAt. That is too weak: a historical migration record - e.g. the clean-machine seed's validation/migrations/old-record.json - has no afterHash and a backupPath pointing at a file that no longer exists, yet it satisfies the filter.

Observed: opening seed-fixable-operator shows 'Safe fixes applied. The original was backed up before any change.' with an Undo migration button, in a session where no migration was applied. Clicking it FAILS SAFE - undoMigration compares digestFor(current) against record.afterHash, which is undefined, so it refuses and nothing is destroyed. But the message tells the user to 'Restore manually from validation\\backups\\seed-fixable-operator-20260201.json', a file that does not exist.

So: not destructive, but a misleading affordance plus a remedy the user cannot follow.

Fix: do not decide undoability in the renderer by absence of undoneAt. Either have validation:migrations return a derived undoable flag from main (afterHash present AND backup file exists AND current digest === afterHash), or filter on those conditions before offering the banner. Prefer the main-side flag - the renderer has neither the digest function nor filesystem access, which is why it guessed.
close_reason:
Fixed 2026-07-30. Undoability is now derived in main by a single predicate, undoBlockedReason(record, current), used by BOTH undoMigration (which throws that sentence) and migrationsForFlow (which reports it as undoable/undoBlockedReason) - so what a surface offers and what the operation permits cannot drift apart, which was the root cause. Blocks on: already undone, flow gone, afterHash not a current digest (the historical-record case), digest mismatch (edited after), and missing backup file. The renderer now filters on record.undoable instead of !record.undoneAt; preload type widened.

verify-legacy-compat 138 -> 152 (14 new checks). Mutation-tested: restoring the old !undoneAt rule fails 6 of them, including the exact reported case (historic-no-afterhash reporting undoable:true). Two of the new checks were initially unreachable because their setup used a flow with no safe fixes - fixed so a setup failure is a hard failure rather than a silent skip. verify-validation 125/0, build clean.

NOT in the packaged artifact: the VM's portable build predates this fix (verify-packaged-validation's freshness guard correctly flags it). Rebuild before any packaged re-verification.

title: Oracle soak: Node peak RSS grows ~5x across a 30-min run (2472MB peak) with no check covering it
description:
SEPARATE from awkit-cww, which was about the leak STATISTIC and is now fixed. This is a distinct failure mode that no invariant currently guards.

Clean idle-host 30-min soak 2026-07-26 (commit dce4204), 18,243,386 queries at 9,746/s, failures=0:

  node RSS series (28 samples, MB):
  137 142 294 199 154 188 499 152 358 | 287 160 281 561 593 849 1289 505 696 | 191 507 954 434 1859 2472 245 1295 1887 1356

  floor (min 1st third -> min last third): 137 -> 245 MB (+108, PASSES the 150MB gate at 72% of budget)
  slope: +52.14 MB/sample = +1460 MB across the run
  endpointDelta: +1219 MB
  peak: 2472 MB

NOT A LEAK: the last third still returns to 245MB, close to the 137MB start, so the process demonstrably still reclaims memory. The floor gate is correct to pass.

THE ACTUAL CONCERN: peak amplitude grows roughly 5x (first third maxes at 499MB; last third hits 1859, 2472, 1887). A 2.4GB transient peak is an OOM risk on a constrained machine and nothing currently fails on it. The floor statistic is the right leak detector but is blind to this by construction.

ALSO: this refutes the concurrent-load confound hypothesis recorded on awkit-cww. The IDLE run is WORSE than the confounded one on every peak-sensitive statistic - slope +1460 vs +1106, endpoint +1219 vs +651, peak 2472 vs 1872. The behaviour is intrinsic, not an artifact of sharing the machine with packaging and GUI verifiers.

SUGGESTED: decide whether a peak-RSS ceiling belongs in the soak invariants, and derive it from a measured baseline rather than from this run. Investigate what allocates so heavily late in a run at ~10k queries/s - one connection is opened and closed per query, so per-query allocation churn is the obvious place to look. The full series is now recorded in reports/oracle-validation/oracle-soak.json (memory.nodeRssSeriesMb) so this can be re-analysed without another 30-minute run.
notes:
2026-07-26 INVESTIGATED. Two root causes, neither of them a product leak. The second one invalidates the SIGNAL both the old and the new check are built on.

CAUSE 1 - THE HARNESS MEASURES ITSELF.
benchmark-oracle-jdbc.mts:185 pushes one element into 'latencies' PER QUERY, unbounded, and :186 does the same for 'dbTimes'. At the clean run's 18,243,386 queries that array alone is 502 MB of LIVE data (measured: survives a forced GC unchanged), against a 30 MB baseline. dbTimes stayed empty in mock mode - the artifact shows dbTimeMs p50=p95=0 - so a LIVE run would roughly double this. The end-of-run [...arr].sort() copies add ~30 MB more. So most of the 'growth' this bead was filed about is the benchmark accumulating its own samples, growing linearly with throughput x duration. It is not the product.

CAUSE 2 - RSS IS NOT A VALID LEAK SIGNAL ON WINDOWS. This is the important one.
process.memoryUsage().rss is the WORKING SET, which the OS trims independently of the process. Measured directly: with an 18.2M-element array live, rss=499MB heapTotal=503MB heapUsed=470MB; after a SetProcessWorkingSetSize trim, rss=5MB while heapUsed stayed 470MB and the array was still fully live. RSS fell 99% with ZERO change in live heap.

That explains the implausible soak samples - 2472MB -> 245MB in 60 seconds is the OS trimming, not the process releasing - and it reconciles the arithmetic that did not previously add up: the last-third floor read 245MB while the latencies array alone had to be ~400-500MB live at that point.

CONSEQUENCE FOR awkit-cww (CLOSED): floor-rise is a genuinely better STATISTIC than the endpoint delta and the negative controls stand, but it is computed over a signal the OS manipulates. A trim landing inside the first window inflates the measured rise; one landing in the last window masks it. The fix was an improvement, not a sound gate, and closing awkit-cww overstated it.

RECOMMENDED, in order:
1. Stop accumulating per-query samples. Use fixed-bucket histograms (1ms buckets to some ceiling + overflow) for the latency/dbTime percentiles - O(1) memory, exact enough for p50/p95/p99, and removes ~500MB of self-inflicted growth. Keep the existing pct() semantics.
2. Gate on heapUsed, not rss. V8's own accounting is immune to working-set trimming (measured above: unchanged across a trim that moved RSS by 494MB). Keep rssTrend() and apply it to the heapUsed series; keep RSS as a DIAGNOSTIC only.
3. Only then decide whether a peak ceiling is still needed - with 1 and 2 done, the remaining signal is finally about the product.

Do NOT simply raise a threshold; the numbers being compared are not the process's memory.
close_reason:
RESOLVED in c6d4547 — and the answer is that there was never a product leak. The growth was the harness measuring itself.

Full 30-minute soak with the fixed harness: 9 PASS / 0 FAIL. 23,458,521 queries at 13,030/s, failures=0, cancellation ok=59 bad=0 p95 252ms, clean teardown.

  node HEAP floor 11 -> 8 MB (rise -3MB), slope +0.08MB/sample (+2MB over the run), peak 24MB
  node RSS  floor 78 -> 78 MB (rise 0), slope 0, peak 80MB
  bridge RSS floor 194 -> 193 MB (-1)

  heap series: 14 11 11 18 14 14 21 20 16 13 12 17 24 16 15 21 13 16 21 13 16 20 20 20 8 18 18 12 19
  rss series : 78 79 79 80 80 79 79 79 79 79 79 79 79 79 79 79 79 79 79 78 78 79 79 79 78 79 79 79 79

Heap oscillates in a tight 8-24MB band with no trend; RSS is flat at 78-80MB for thirty minutes.

Same workload, before vs after the harness fix:
  peak RSS      2472MB -> 80MB
  throughput    9,746/s -> 13,030/s (+34%)
  max latency   36,727ms -> 4,681ms

The +34% throughput and the collapse in max latency are the tell: the harness was spending roughly a third of the machine on its own accounting, and the multi-second latency outliers were GC pauses from the per-minute [...latencies].sort() over an array holding one entry per query.

NUANCE worth recording rather than overstating: with the harness fixed, RSS is stable enough that it would have carried the verdict fine. The Windows working-set finding (rss can fall 99% with heapUsed unchanged) is real and measured, and moving the verdict to heapUsed is still correct because a trim CAN corrupt an RSS verdict while heap cannot be trimmed - but cause 1 (the harness) was the dominant one. Cause 2 is why the numbers never reconciled, not why the gate broke.

No peak-RSS ceiling is being added: with the harness fixed there is nothing left to ceiling. Revisit only if a future run shows peak growth against a flat heap.

title: benchmark:oracle-jdbc Node RSS leak check fails; endpoint-delta method cannot distinguish a leak from GC sawtooth
description:
RED GATE, reported truthfully - do NOT loosen the threshold to make it pass.

Run 2026-07-26 at 94c858e: 8 passed, 1 failed. Failing check: 'Node (Specter) RSS did not leak (drift < 150MB)' - drift=651MB over 28 samples (start 104MB, end 755MB). Everything else passed: full 30.2 min, 19,659,232 queries at 10,864.8/s, failures=0, cancellation ok=56 bad=0 p95=251ms, bridge (Java) RSS drift -37MB, pending=0, no orphan Java, no pool metrics.

METHOD WEAKNESS: scripts/benchmark-oracle-jdbc.mts:246 computes rssDrift = nodeRss[last] - nodeRss[0], a two-point endpoint delta, then line 288 compares abs() against 150. It ignores the other 26 samples. The observed series is a strong sawtooth: 104 126 159 319 138 363 521 328 328 53 ... 745 1286 827 1872 755. It DIPS TO 53MB at t+10.3m, BELOW the 104MB start - a monotonic leak cannot decrease, so the process demonstrably returns memory. But the peaks do rise (521 -> 745 -> 1286 -> 1872), so growth in the high-water mark is NOT ruled out. The endpoint delta would have 'passed' had the final sample landed in a trough, so the check is close to arbitrary on this signal.

CONFOUND: this run shared the machine with electron-builder packaging, Electron GUI verifiers and Chromium workloads. Re-run on an otherwise-idle host before drawing conclusions.

SUGGESTED FIX (owner decision - changing the method while the gate is red risks moving the goalposts): replace the endpoint delta with a trend statistic (least-squares slope over all samples, or median of the first quartile vs the last quartile), derive the threshold from a MEASURED idle-host baseline, and record how it was measured so the next person raises it rather than lowering it to match a failure. Consider also recording the high-water mark separately from the trend.

NOT caused by this session's changes (manualApproval routing, packaging staleness guard, validate-offline output, mock-site fixture) - none touch Oracle JDBC or memory. The artifact reports/oracle-validation/oracle-soak.json is untracked, so there is no committed baseline to diff against.
notes:
2026-07-26 FOLLOW-UP — closing this was premature in one respect. See awkit-q0e.

The floor-rise statistic is a real improvement over the endpoint delta and its 10 negative controls stand. But it is computed over process.memoryUsage().rss, and RSS on Windows is the WORKING SET, which the OS trims independently of the process. Measured: an 18.2M-element array live gave rss=499MB / heapUsed=470MB; after a SetProcessWorkingSetSize trim, rss=5MB while heapUsed was UNCHANGED at 470MB and the array was still fully live.

So a trim landing inside the first sampling window inflates the measured floor rise, and one landing in the last window masks it. The gate is better than what it replaced but is not yet sound. The remedy (gate on heapUsed, keep RSS as a diagnostic) is tracked on awkit-q0e together with the harness's unbounded per-query sample arrays, which contribute ~502MB of the observed growth by themselves.

Leaving this CLOSED because the statistic change it describes is done and committed in dce4204; the signal change is a separate piece of work.
close_reason:
Fixed in dce4204. The check now gates on FLOOR RISE (min last third - min first third) with the original 150MB/200MB budgets unchanged - a change of statistic, not a relaxation. Verified on a clean idle-host 30-min soak: 9 PASS / 0 FAIL. Node floor 137->245MB (+108, 72% of budget); bridge floor 157->156MB (-1). Negative-controlled 10/10 before the run.

Two corrections recorded for the next reader: (1) the trend statistics made the ORIGINAL failure MORE credible, not less - my earlier 'endpoint delta is close to arbitrary' framing was wrong in the exonerating direction; (2) the concurrent-load confound hypothesis is REFUTED - the idle run is worse than the confounded one on slope (+1460 vs +1106), endpoint (+1219 vs +651) and peak (2472 vs 1872).

title: dependency-manifest builtAt conflates manifest regeneration with payload provenance
description:
`resources/dependency-manifest.json` has a single `application.builtAt` field that records when the
MANIFEST was regenerated -- but readers naturally interpret it as the vintage of the bundled
runtime payload it describes.

Observed concretely during the 61f6099 artifact regeneration (2026-07-22):
  application.builtAt = 2026-07-22T20:47:18Z   <- manifest regeneration (this build)
  browsers[0].version = 149.0.7827.55          <- payload actually dated 2026-07-10

`generate-dependency-manifest.ps1` rewrites the file on every `package:portable` run, so builtAt
tracks the build, never the payload. Anyone auditing provenance from this manifest would date the
Chromium payload 12 days later than it is.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Manifest metadata distinguishes manifest generation from payload provenance, with explicit
   separate fields, e.g.:
     manifestGeneratedAt     - when THIS manifest was written
     browserPayloadBuiltAt   - when the browser payload was produced / obtained
     browserPayloadSource    - how it was obtained, including the version requested
     browserPayloadHash      - hash of the copied payload
2. `builtAt` must NOT imply the age of Chromium or of any other copied dependency. Either rename
   it, or restrict its documented meaning to manifest generation alone.
3. Existing readers of `builtAt` keep working, or are updated in the same change.
4. The distinction is documented wherever artifact provenance is recorded.
5. Payload provenance fields are what artifact comparison and runbook pinning rely on -- see
   awkit-epz criteria 7-8: while a build-time timestamp remains embedded in a packaged file,
   whole-artifact hash equality cannot be used as reproducibility evidence.
notes: Split out of awkit-epz so that bead stays focused on reproducibility. This one is metadata naming/semantics only -- smaller scope, no packaging behaviour change. Evidence: C:\Users\moham\awkit-build-evidence\61f6099\provenance.md
close_reason: Manifest schema v2 replaces ambiguous application.builtAt with top-level manifestGeneratedAt and records Chromium payload source, requested/installed Playwright versions, a source timestamp with basis, and a deterministic sha256-tree-v1 digest. Existing validators/readers and provenance docs were updated; strict offline validation passes and a digest mutation fails.

title: Successful runs log browser cleanup as execution-failed-cleanup
description:
`PlaywrightRunner.executeScenario`'s `finally` block closes the runtime with the hardcoded reason
"execution-failed-cleanup" on EVERY exit path, including success
(src/runner/PlaywrightRunner.ts:282). A passing run's structured log therefore reads:

    [browser:g1] closing runtime (execution-failed-cleanup).

which actively misleads anyone reading run logs to debug a failure.

SCOPE -- READ THIS BEFORE ESTIMATING IMPACT:
This corrects MISLEADING STRUCTURED RUN-LOG TEXT ONLY. It does NOT affect shared-browser
close-reason analytics, lifecycle buckets, crash-rate backpressure, or capacity decisions.

Verified: `BrowserCloseReason` (PlaywrightRunner.ts:32) reaches exactly two places -- the log line
at PlaywrightRunner.ts:402, and `onRuntimeClosing`, whose SOLE consumer (ExecutionEngine.ts:1334)
destructures `({ generation })` and DISCARDS the reason. It is a DIFFERENT enum from
`SharedBrowserCloseReason` (SharedBrowserPool.ts:48), which is what actually feeds
runtime_browser_lifecycle_buckets and BrowserPoolEffectiveness.closeReasons via
RuntimeObservationCollector. The two enums never meet.

An earlier draft of the SRS claimed analytics contamination; tracing the consumers disproved it.
Do not reintroduce that claim.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Add `execution-completed-cleanup` to the BrowserCloseReason union and use it ONLY for successful
   terminal cleanup.
2. The failure path keeps `execution-failed-cleanup`.
3. Do NOT rename existing members. `app-shutdown` and `reuse-session-swap-old-runtime` stay as-is --
   renaming churns existing log-grep habits for no behavioural gain.
4. Only add `execution-cancelled-cleanup` if it is genuinely distinguished from the existing
   `user-request`, which the cancel path already uses; otherwise reuse `user-request`.
5. Do NOT add a `browser-crash` member. `onRuntimeClosing` is documented as announcing INTENTIONAL
   teardown so the pool does not score it as a crash; a crash reason on that channel inverts the
   semantics that keep crash-rate backpressure honest.
6. Regression test asserts a successful run logs `execution-completed-cleanup` and a failed run
   logs `execution-failed-cleanup`.
7. The change note explicitly states there is NO analytics or capacity impact, and does NOT claim
   close-reason distributions will shift.
notes: Spec: docs/SRS_BROWSER_AUTOMATION_OBSERVABILITY.md FR-G1 change-dependency (Tranche 0). Low risk, but becomes load-bearing once FR-A2 puts lifecycle events on the unified timeline -- fix before the CDP work, not after.

title: Numeric record-to-replay fidelity gate for the recorder (measured %, not just pass/fail)
description:
Idea sourced from the 2026-07-22 browser-automation skills teardown
(BROWSER_AUTOMATION_SKILLS_REPORT.md sections 2A and 5). Reference implementation:
ruvnet/ruflo `browser-replay` + scripts/replay-spike.sh.

THE PATTERN WORTH STEALING: ruflo treats "is a recorded session actually replayable?" as
a MEASURED NUMBER, not a boolean. Their ADR-0001 will not move Proposed -> Accepted until
a spike demonstrates >=80% replay success across 10 distinct sites of varying DOM-drift
profiles. Per-run verdict = matched-steps / total-steps against a tolerance (default 0.85).
That converts a vague architectural bet into a ship gate.

CURRENT AWKIT STATE (verified):
- verify:recorder-flow tests recorded-actions -> flow SHAPE (Start/End nodes, wiring,
  waits as fixed-time, tab switches as Route Change). Pure logic, no browser.
- verify:recorder-locator, verify:recorder-draft, verify:flow-step-mapping cover locator
  generation, draft persistence, and round-trip serialization respectively.
- verify:runner does live checks against the mock site.
- What is MISSING: an end-to-end record -> replay loop that produces a FIDELITY
  PERCENTAGE across the mock-site scenario set. Today a replay either passes or fails a
  scenario; there is no aggregate number to watch for regression.

PROPOSED:
1. Harness that, for each applicable mock-site scenario, records a flow, replays it, and
   scores matched-steps / total-steps.
2. Emit an aggregate fidelity percentage plus a per-scenario table, so a drop is visible
   as a number rather than as one flipped assertion.
3. Pick a threshold and enforce it. ruflo chose 0.80 aggregate / 0.85 per-run; AWKIT's
   number should be set from a first baseline run, not copied.
4. Deliberately include drift-y scenarios so the metric has headroom to detect regression
   (the mock site is the Feature Test Lab - extend it per mock-site-maintainer).

WHY THIS MATTERS HERE: the randomized-test-lab round-trip work already proved that silent
fidelity loss is AWKIT's recurring failure mode (13 round-trip defects, awkit-cxa's bare
FlowStep.value drop). Those were each found by a targeted assertion after the fact. A
standing fidelity number would have shown the regression as a trend.

GOTCHAS FROM THE SOURCE MATERIAL:
- Network/timing nondeterminism produces false-fail verdicts. Pin to mock-site fixtures

title: Async engine: grouped completion composition (A AND (B OR C))

title: Recorder: redundant fill echo recorded after focus leaves a field
