title: Recorder: remote (non-adjacent) hover triggers are not attributed
description:
Boundary left open by awkit-vot (adjacent-sibling hover attribution).

resolveSiblingHoverTrigger in src/recorder/recorderInitScript.ts attributes a hover-gated click only when the trigger is an ADJACENT SIBLING of the revealed surface (the relationship '.trigger:hover + .target' encodes). A reveal driven from a DIFFERENT subtree - e.g. a JS 'mouseenter' on a control in one wrapper that shows a control in another - is neither an ancestor nor a sibling, so it is classified 'none': no hover step, and the recorded click can fail replay because the target is hidden until the remote trigger is hovered.

This is deliberate, not an oversight. Reveal-moment pointer evidence IS available for these cases (the revealWitness WeakMap records where the pointer was when a hidden-at-rest control was first seen visible), but on its own that evidence is weak: any hover that coincides with any reveal anywhere on the page satisfies it. Adjacency is what makes the joint evidence strong enough to persist a trigger.

Pinned as current behaviour by scripts/verify-recorder-hover.mts section [12c] against the mock-site fixture .remote-trigger-j5w1 / .remote-gated-j5w1 (/recorder-lab). Dropping the adjacency requirement makes that section fail - verified by mutation.

Follow-up: find a second independent signal that upgrades remote pointer evidence to attributable (e.g. correlating the reveal with a mouseenter listener on the witness, or a confirmed re-hover), or emit needs-review instead of silently dropping the prerequisite.
close_reason: Remote (non-adjacent) hover triggers are now attributed and replayed. The fix removes an inconsistency rather than adding a signal: a remote hover that INSERTS a control has been attributed since awkit-0vm (the insertion resolver never required adjacency), while one that merely unhides an existing control was refused on identical evidence. revealWitness now records {el, since, at, cause}, and resolveRemoteHoverTrigger requires a concrete witness, cause=pointer, the pointer's ARRIVAL within INSERTION_CAUSAL_WINDOW_MS of the reveal, the witness outside the revealed surface, still connected, still the pointer owner at click time, and a stable locator from the shared buildTriggerLocator. Chained after the sibling path, so it can only turn none into trigger/review. verify:recorder-hover 211/211 incl. two-fresh-page replay and click-alone-fails. Mutations with focused failures: remote attribution disabled, reveal-witness removed, arrival window removed. NOT covered on the remote path: competing-cause filter and witness-outside-surface (both covered on the insertion path). Filed awkit-a7k for the harness install-order gap found on the way.

title: Recorder: controls inserted only after hover lack hidden-at-rest evidence (Inc5 residual)
description: Increment 5 hover-dependency capture records first-seen (rest) visibility at the recorder's baseline scan. A control (or its container) that is inserted into the DOM only AFTER a hover is never observed hidden-at-rest, so resolveHoverTrigger cannot attribute the reveal and no hover prerequisite is produced. Deliberate 'don't fabricate' trade-off. Follow-up: use MutationObserver insertion timing + pointer trail to attribute hover-inserted controls, or mark needs-review.
close_reason: Shadow-internal hover triggers now persist the INTERNAL control, not its host. buildTriggerLocator emits the Increment 6 shape for a trigger inside an open shadow root: ordered outer-to-inner context.shadow.hosts plus a semantic locator generated against the innermost root, strictly unique within it, non-positional, no XPath - resolved by the existing LocatorFactory (no new executor, no piercing selector). A host locator is persisted only when the host itself was the observed pointer witness; an unrepresentable inner trigger degrades to needs-review with 'hover trigger inside open shadow root could not be represented safely' and no executable fallback. Root cause of the wrong witness: event.target is retargeted to the host on a window-level capture listener, so recordPointer now uses the composed path. Regression fixture uses nested open roots whose hosts are far larger than the corner-pinned trigger with the listener on the trigger, so hovering a host inserts nothing; a light-DOM decoy sharing the trigger's accessible name makes the host chain load-bearing. verify:recorder-hover 191/191. Mutations producing focused failures: inner witness->host, shadow context dropped, host order reversed, strict inner uniqueness removed. The :nth-* regex on the inner locator is defence-in-depth and NOT independently observable (the generator marks unresolvable inner targets quality.strategy=fallback first) - kept, and reported as uncovered rather than claimed.

title: Recorder: sibling/self-toggle hover triggers not attributed (Inc5 residual)
description: Increment 5 (awkit-aui.5) hover-dependency capture attributes a reveal only when the click target has a hidden-at-rest ANCESTOR container (resolveHoverTrigger in src/recorder/recorderInitScript.ts). A sibling/self-toggle trigger such as '.trigger:hover + .target { display:block }' — where the revealed control has no hidden ancestor container — is intentionally classified 'none' (no hover step) rather than review, to avoid fabricating a trigger. Such a recorded click can still fail replay because the control is hidden until the sibling is hovered. Deliberate 'don't fabricate' trade-off; not covered by the mock. New resolveSiblingHoverTrigger runs when the ancestor walk finds no hidden ancestor run, and as a fallback when it would return review. Four joint guards, each mutation-proven load-bearing: last-sample-outside-the-reveal, adjacency to the revealed root, a revealWitness recording where the pointer was when the control was first seen visible (separates a hover-caused reveal from a coincident timer), and the existing non-positional stability bar. verify:recorder-hover 81/81 (was 48/48), including replay through the real StepExecutor. title: Run reports omit Legacy Compatibility attribution
description:
Found during clean-machine runbook 5.4 on 2026-07-29 (results doc: docs/testing/CLEAN_MACHINE_VALIDATION_RESULTS_2026-07-29.md, fifth sitting).

A workflow run that is admitted ONLY because the flow holds a Legacy Compatibility grant completes and reports 'passed' with no indication anywhere in the run report that a grant was involved. Verified on a clean machine: reports/<id>.json and reports/<id>/report.json contain no 'legacy', 'compatib' or 'grant' token at all.

The attribution exists, but only on the grant record: app/main/validation/flowValidationService.ts recordRunUnderCompatibility() increments runsUnderCompatibility and stamps lastRunAt. That is a sound audit trail, but an operator reading a run report cannot tell that the run only executed under a compatibility grant.

Proposed: carry the grant-admitted flow ids (and their grant deadlines) into the execution report and the run detail UI, so a run that depended on Legacy Compatibility says so. Keep it derived from the grant standing at admission time, not persisted separately.

Not a security defect - the gate itself behaved correctly (5.8/8.2 pass: no grant permits an active-path break).

A run admitted only because a flow holds a Legacy Compatibility grant now says so in its execution report. New optional ConcurrentRunReport.legacyCompatibility carries each admitted flow's id, name and grant deadline; it is ABSENT on ordinary runs, so its presence is itself the attribution and an empty grant list is omitted rather than written as an empty block. Modelled on the existing 'security' block, which exists for the same reason: a run admitted by an exemption must not look identical to one that passed the validator outright.

Snapshotted AT ADMISSION, not re-derived at read time, exactly as the bead asked: execution.ipc.ts already derived compatibilityFlowIds from the validation issues at the run gate, and now also reads grantsMap() there for the deadlines and puts the result on ConcurrentRunProfile.legacyCompatibility. ExecutionEngine passes it into ReportService.createConcurrentRunReport. Grants expire and are revoked, so a historical report must keep saying what was true when the run started.

New npm run verify:run-report-compatibility (21/21, class unit): builds reports through the real ReportService, asserts the token scan the clean-machine runbook used actually finds 'legacy'/'compatib'/the flow id in the serialized report, asserts an ordinary run contains none of them, covers multiple flows keeping distinct deadlines, and carries source guards over the admission -> profile -> engine -> report chain. Four mutations produce focused failures: report drops the block (5); engine stops passing it (1); block written unconditionally (1); admission stops snapshotting grants (2). That last guard first passed for the wrong reason - an unqualified /grantsMap\(\)/ match was satisfied by an unrelated call elsewhere in the same file - and was tightened to the specific assignment.

SCOPE NOTE: the run-detail UI is NOT covered. The Reports drawer reads telemetry.runDetail from the durable SQLite store, so surfacing it there needs a schema migration; filed separately rather than bundled here. verify-legacy-compat.mts 152/152 (run directly - it has no npm script, which is worth fixing), telemetry 61/61, runner 89/89, reports GUI 31/31, ipc-contract 5/5 all green.

title: oracle-soak.json is silently overwritten by a short run — no duration guard on the release-gate artifact
description:
benchmark-oracle-jdbc.mts writes reports/oracle-validation/oracle-soak.json on EVERY invocation regardless of AWKIT_ORACLE_SOAK_MINUTES. A 2- or 4-minute smoke run replaces the 30-minute release evidence in place, with nothing in the filename or the surrounding docs to signal it.

This actually happened on 2026-07-26: after a 4-minute smoke run the canonical artifact read durationMinutes=4 / 2.9M queries while the docs referenced it as the 30-minute soak evidence. It was caught by chance when a killed background run prompted a manual check, not by any guard.

Same class as the packaged-tree staleness defect (HARNESS-008): an artifact that looks authoritative but describes something other than what the reader assumes. That one is now guarded by a precondition that refuses to run; this one is not.

Also note a related trap: a run shorter than two samples passes the memory invariants TRIVIALLY, because a trend needs two points. A short smoke run therefore both overwrites the evidence AND reports a green memory gate that proves nothing.

SUGGESTED: either (a) refuse to overwrite the canonical path when SOAK_MINUTES is below the release-gate duration, writing to a clearly-marked scratch path instead; or (b) include the duration in the filename and have the docs reference the full-length artifact explicitly. Whichever is chosen, the memory invariants should report NOT RUN rather than PASS when there are fewer than two samples.
close_reason:
Fixed and negative-controlled. Two independent guards in scripts/benchmark-oracle-jdbc.mts:

1. ARTIFACT PATH. Only a run with AWKIT_ORACLE_SOAK_MINUTES >= RELEASE_GATE_MINUTES (30) writes the canonical reports/oracle-validation/oracle-soak.json. A shorter run writes oracle-soak-SHORT-<n>min.json and prints a banner: 'SMOKE RUN (n min < 30 min). This is NOT the release gate: the canonical ... was NOT written, and the result above must not be cited as soak evidence.'

2. MEMORY VERDICT. New checkTrend() reports NOT RUN, not PASS, when a series has fewer than MIN_MEMORY_SAMPLES (2). rssFloorWithinBudget returns true below two samples because a trend is UNDEFINED there, not because the process behaved - counting that as a pass is exactly how a short run reported a green memory gate that proved nothing. The tally now reads e.g. '7 passed, 0 failed, 2 NOT RUN'.

VERIFIED with a real 1-minute run against a canonical artifact holding the 30-min result:
  - tally: 7 passed, 0 failed, 2 NOT RUN (was: 9 passed, 0 failed)
  - both memory invariants printed '~ ... NOT RUN: 0 sample(s), needs 2 for a trend'
  - artifact written to oracle-soak-SHORT-1min.json
  - canonical oracle-soak.json BYTE-IDENTICAL afterwards (md5 54296276e02ecfaf75308ff9056e2af1, still durationMinutes=30.01 / 23,458,521 queries)
  - smoke-run banner printed

Note recorded in the file header: reports/ is gitignored, so this artifact is local evidence only and was never in version control - which lowers the blast radius of the original defect but does not remove it, since the docs cite the file by path.

title: Locator recovery memory: remember the winning candidate, recover when all recorded candidates miss
description:
Idea sourced from the 2026-07-22 browser-automation skills teardown
(BROWSER_AUTOMATION_SKILLS_REPORT.md sections 2A and 5). Reference implementation:
ruvnet/ruflo AgentDB `browser-selectors` namespace, keyed <host>:<intent> ->
{selector, ref, snapshot-hash, last-success}, recovered at replay time by embedding
similarity.

CURRENT AWKIT STATE (verified in src/runner/LocatorFactory.ts resolve()):
AWKIT already does the hard part, and arguably better than the reference:
  1. container/frame context so candidates resolve inside the right subtree
  2. primary candidate, then `alternatives` in recorded order
  3. unique match wins; else the single VISIBLE match wins; else single ENABLED;
     else single IN-VIEWPORT; never guesses between equally-actionable twins
  4. all-counts-zero returns the primary so the caller's action auto-waits
  5. genuinely ambiguous -> clear diagnostic via formatFailure
Alternatives are carried on the node (recorderInitScript.buildAlternatives) rather than
looked up at replay time.

THE ACTUAL GAP - two things the recorded-alternatives design cannot do:
(a) NO RECOVERY WHEN EVERY RECORDED CANDIDATE MISSES. Once the primary and all
    alternatives resolve to zero, the step fails. There is no similarity fallback to a
    structurally-near element.
(b) NO LEARNING. Which candidate actually won last run is discarded. A flow whose primary
    has been dead for months still pays the full miss-then-fallback cost every run, and
    nothing records that the site drifted.

PROPOSED (incremental, offline - no embeddings service, no network):
1. Persist last-success per step: which candidate index resolved, plus a cheap structural
   fingerprint of the matched element. Reorder candidates by last-success on the next run.
   This is (b) alone and is low-risk.
2. Only if (1) proves insufficient: a local similarity fallback when all candidates miss -
   score visible elements against the recorded fingerprint (role/name/text/attrs/ancestry)
   and accept a match only above a high threshold, logging loudly that recovery fired.

HARD CONSTRAINTS:
- Offline-first: no embedding model, no remote vector store. Structural/lexical similarity
  computed locally, or nothing.
- Preserve the existing invariant from LocatorFactory: recovery may only convert
  would-be FAILURES into successes. It must never change which element an
  already-unambiguous step resolves to. Any similarity path must run strictly AFTER the
  all-candidates-missed branch.
- Never emit or match on utility/hashed classes (established recorder rule).
- Recovery firing is a signal the flow needs a re-record. Surface it, do not silently heal
  forever.

VERIFY: verify:recorder-locator for candidate ordering and fingerprinting (pure logic);
verify:runner for the live miss-then-recover path. Feeds the fidelity metric in awkit-60w.
notes: Implemented durable per-scenario/flow/step winner memory plus privacy-preserving class-free structural fingerprinting (visible text/labels/attribute values are token-hashed before persistence). Saved winner is tried first. Local recovery runs only after every recorded candidate misses and a bounded recheck, scans <=200 visible elements, requires >=0.86 score and >=0.08 unique margin, logs loudly, and tells the user to re-record. Verified: npm run verify:recorder 110/110; npm run verify:runner 89/89; mutation threshold 1.01 produced 107/110 and was reverted.

title: Instance Monitor: second read-only CDP observation client + on-disk run trace
description:
Idea sourced from the 2026-07-22 browser-automation skills teardown
(BROWSER_AUTOMATION_SKILLS_REPORT.md sections 2E and 5). Reference implementation:
Browserbase `skills/browser-trace`.

KEYSTONE FACT: every Chrome DevTools target accepts MULTIPLE concurrent CDP clients.
So an observation client can attach to a target that the runner is already driving,
enable only observation domains (Network, Console, Runtime, Log, Page), and never send
action commands. Non-intrusive by construction.

CURRENT AWKIT GAP (verified): no surface attaches a CDP client for observation.
src/session/SessionCaptureService.ts is explicitly "No CDP connection"; the
https-certificate-trust work confirmed AWKIT has only two context factories and no
CDP attach path. Instance Monitor (app/renderer/pages/InstanceMonitor.tsx,
verify:instance-monitor + verify:instance-monitor-gui) shows run state but has no
event firehose or live browser view.

PROPOSED (offline-safe, all local):
1. Observation-only CDP client attached to a running instance's Chromium. Never issues
   actions. Fails open - if attach fails the run is unaffected.
2. On-disk run trace under the existing artifacts root (NOT resources/, NOT app.asar),
   modelled on Browserbase's .o11y/<run-id>/ layout:
     manifest.json          run metadata, target, domains, started/stopped
     index.jsonl            one line per sample {ts, screenshot, dom, url}
     cdp/raw.ndjson         firehose, one JSON object per line
     cdp/summary.json       session totals + per-page domains/network/timing
     cdp/<bucket>/*.jsonl   network / console / runtime / log / page buckets
     cdp/pages/<pid>/       per-page slices, bisected on top-level Page.frameNavigated
     screenshots/<ts>.png, dom/<ts>.html
   summary.json is the analysis entry point.
3. Live browser viewing in Instance Monitor built on the same attach.

WHY IT FITS AWKIT: the layout is a filesystem tree with zero network dependency, so it
survives the offline-first constraint that rules out the cloud live_url / debugger_url
approach that browser-use and Browserbase use.

SCOPE NOTE: distinct from awkit-4km, which covers CDP diagnostics for *wait/async
resolution* (redirect chains, timing, request ids) inside the runner. This bead is the
*observability* surface: a passive tracer plus its persisted artifact plus the monitor UI.
Coordinate so both share one attach helper rather than opening two clients.

GOTCHAS FROM THE SOURCE MATERIAL:
- Do not poll screenshots/DOM faster than ~1s; 2s is the recommended default.
- Adding the DOM domain is very noisy - opt-in only.
- Always run the stop path even after a crash, or background samplers linger.
- rrweb-style DOM replay is deprecated upstream; screenshot + DOM timeline is the
  accepted visual ground truth. Do not build on rrweb.
- Retention/size policy needed: raw.ndjson grows fast. Reuse the artifacts retention
  path (verify:artifacts).

VERIFY: extend verify:instance-monitor for the trace shape and bisection, and
verify:artifacts for retention. Bisection is pure logic and can be tested without a browser.
notes: Implemented a fail-open, observation-only second CDP client with an explicit command allowlist, 2s bounded visual sampling, opt-in DOM capture, secret-redacted/capped raw NDJSON, idempotent 17-bucket and per-navigation-page bisection, durable trace artifact, and a permission-gated Instance Monitor live view. Verified: instance monitor 55/55, artifacts 23/23, real Electron GUI 18/18, runner 89/89, build PASS. Mutation: temporarily allowlisted Input.dispatchMouseEvent; focused gate failed 54/55, then reverted and passed 55/55.
close_reason: Passive CDP observation trace and live Instance Monitor view implemented and verified.

title: Flow Designer GUI: compact-viewport Node Properties geometry check is intermittent
description:
Observed 2026-08-02 while verifying awkit-x48.

scripts/verify-flow-designer-gui.mjs check 'Node Properties remains a right-edge overlay inside the canvas when the toolbar wraps at a compact viewport' failed once at 1024x768 with:
  canvasRight 1024, panelRight 1018.57, panelLeft 580.67, bodyPaddingRight 6

It did not reproduce: two subsequent runs of the same working tree were 72/72, and a run at clean HEAD (before the awkit-x48 change) was 69/69. So it is not attributable to that change.

Most likely a settle race: the check measures panel geometry immediately after a viewport resize, and a fractional-pixel layout can be mid-transition. Suggested fix: wait for a stable measurement (two consecutive identical bounding boxes, or an explicit transition end) before asserting, rather than widening the tolerance - widening would weaken a check that is meant to catch the panel escaping the canvas.

Low priority, but worth fixing: an intermittent in a release gate trains people to re-run instead of read.
notes:
2026-08-02 (Claude Code) — INVESTIGATED, NOT FIXED. No code shipped; the verifier is back at its committed state. Re-scoping: this is not a simple flake.

ROOT CAUSE, measured in the real app. The two resize-based geometry checks do:
  await win.setViewportSize(...); await win.waitForTimeout(180); readInspectorGeometry(win)
Resizing re-mounts the inspector, which runs 'awkit-config-drawer-in' for 240ms from
translateX(16px) scale(0.99) with animation-fill-mode: both. The fixed 180ms wait therefore samples
DURING that animation. Live probe:
  at sample time: transform matrix(0.99,0,0,0.99,16,0), panelRight 1025.8  (outside canvasRight 1024)
  1500ms later:   transform matrix(1,0,0,1,0,0),        panelRight 1012    (correctly inside)
  animation: awkit-config-drawer-in, 240ms, fill both, finished at identity
So the panel's final position is CORRECT. There is no 1.8px overflow defect.

WHAT I TRIED, AND WHY IT WAS WRONG. First attempt polled until two consecutive geometry reads were
identical. That made the failure DETERMINISTIC in the wrong direction: fill-mode 'both' holds the FROM
frame perfectly still before the animation starts, so 'two equal samples' is satisfied by the
pre-animation state. Same trap class as a guard satisfied by the failure state's own steady period.

Second attempt awaited document.getAnimations() then two rAFs. Panel geometry then reads correctly
(panelLeft 572, panelRight 1012, width 440 — exactly its slot). But TWO checks then fail, because the
settled layout is not what the assertions expect:
  settled:        canvasEngineWidth 332, canvasWidth 784, bodyPaddingRight 452
  mid-animation:  canvasEngineWidth 784, canvasWidth 784, bodyPaddingRight 0
The assertion requires Math.abs(canvasEngineWidth - canvasWidth) <= 2 — i.e. a FLOATING OVERLAY where
the engine keeps full width. Settled, '.designer-layout.has-right-panel .flow-designer-body' applies
padding-right: calc(--awkit-active-drawer-width + --space-3) = 452px, so the canvas is INSET instead.
Note the first (non-resize) measurement at line ~436 waits 360ms and PASSES the overlay assertion, so
overlay-vs-inset appears to differ before and after a resize.

THE OPEN QUESTION IS A DESIGN ONE, not a test one: after a viewport resize, should the Node
Properties inspector float over a full-width canvas (what the assertions encode, and what the first
measurement observes) or inset the canvas by the drawer width (what the settled post-resize layout
does)? Answer that and the fix follows — either correct the layout, or correct two assertions that
were calibrated against a transient frame.

ALSO FOUND: this verifier has more than one intermittent. With the file at its committed state a
later run failed a different check — 'GUI 4km persists SSE observation without promoting it to a
completion gate' — while the geometry check passed. Observed totals across this session: 69/69,
72/72 (x3), 71/72 (geometry), 70/72 (SSE). Worth treating as a suite-level timing problem.

Suggested next step: decide the overlay-vs-inset question, then land the getAnimations() wait
(waiting on what actually moves is right regardless) together with whichever side needs correcting.
close_reason:
Root cause was NOT a flake in the sense the bead assumed - it was a fixed-delay race against two independent async layout mechanisms, and the settled design is INSET (owner decision), not the floating-overlay model awkit-9p6 shipped in 2026-07-18.

Measured live: opening/resizing the Node Properties drawer triggers a CSS transition on .flow-designer-body's padding-right (declared 240ms, measured only ~87% complete at 500ms) plus a ResizeObserver-driven --awkit-action-bar-h update (not a CSS animation, invisible to getAnimations()). A fixed waitForTimeout(180/360) could sample either a mid-transition frame (looking like overlay: canvasEngineWidth==canvasWidth) or the settled frame (inset: canvasEngineRight==panelLeft exactly, measured at 3 viewports) - the SAME code intermittently produced both, which is why the compact-viewport check specifically flaked rather than failing cleanly.

Fix: new waitForDrawerSettled() helper awaits Animation.finished on the drawer subtree (covers both the CSS transition and the panel's own awkit-config-drawer-in keyframe), then polls geometry to two identical consecutive reads to catch the ResizeObserver settle too - safe here because nothing holds a frozen pre-transition frame (unlike an animation-fill-mode:both keyframe), so equal reads mean arrival, not a frozen start state. All three overlay-shaped assertions (default open, 1936x1290, 1024x768) rewritten to the inset invariant: canvasEngineWidth < canvasWidth-4 AND canvasEngineRight <= panelLeft+2. Stale overlay-model comments corrected in the same file and in docs/ai/CURRENT_STATE.md (which explicitly superseded the awkit-9p6 entry).

Verified: 72/72 across 4 consecutive runs (was flaking 70-71/72). Mutation-tested the fix itself: injected 'padding-right: 0 !important' via addStyleTag to simulate a regression back to overlay - all three new assertions correctly failed (69/72), proving they are load-bearing, not vacuous. Reverted the injection, re-confirmed 72/72. Also fixed a stale 'overlays the full-width canvas' comment on the unrelated collapse check (logic untouched, was already using an observable waitForFunction). Toolbar-wrap and compact-viewport behavior untouched - only the geometry ASSERTIONS and the wait strategy changed, never the app's CSS/layout code. SSE completion-gate intermittent noted separately in a prior investigation was NOT touched here (different check, different root cause - out of scope).

Gates: verify:flow-designer 72/72 (x4); verify:source-hygiene 9/9; roadmap dashboard 156/156 (Sources agree, after adding the ledger tally to the new CURRENT_STATE.md section - the same 'newest section must quote the tally' trap as before); git diff --check clean.

title: Undo-refusal toast leaks the IPC channel name
description:
Found during clean-machine runbook 8.11 on 2026-07-30 (results doc: docs/testing/CLEAN_MACHINE_VALIDATION_RESULTS_2026-07-29.md, sixth sitting).

Refusing an unsafe undo produces the right message, but it reaches the user wrapped in Electron's remote-method preamble:

  Error invoking remote method 'validation:undoMigration': Error: Flow seed-fixable-operator was edited after this migration - undo would destroy those changes. Restore manually from <path> if intended.

The domain sentence is correct, specific and actionable; only the wrapper should go. FlowChartDesigner.undoLastMigration surfaces error.message directly, and for an ipcRenderer.invoke rejection that message already contains the channel name.

Proposed: strip the Error invoking remote method '<channel>': Error:  prefix at the renderer boundary (one shared helper - the same wrapper will affect every other invoke-backed toast, so fix it once rather than per call site).

Cosmetic; no behaviour change. The refusal itself is correct: the migration was left with no undoneAt, the later edit was preserved, and the backup was retained.
close_reason:
Fixed at the single renderer-facing IPC boundary. New app/main/ipcErrorMessage.ts strips Electron's "Error invoking remote method '<channel>': " preamble (anchored, so a domain sentence quoting it is untouched; bounded unwrapping for nested preambles) and then only the GENERIC 'Error: ' name - TypeError/RangeError are preserved because they signal a bug rather than a considered refusal. Empty or non-Error rejections fall back instead of showing a blank toast. preload.ts gained an invoke() wrapper that routes every rejection through it and keeps the original as 'cause' so the failing channel survives for diagnostics; all 202 call sites now use it, and the wrapper is the only remaining direct ipcRenderer.invoke. No renderer change was needed - FlowChartDesigner.undoLastMigration already surfaces error.message, which is now clean, and every other invoke-backed toast is fixed at the same time.

Proved in the real app, not just in a unit: verify:flow-designer now asserts that a rejected validation:undoMigration call reaches the renderer as 'No migration no-such-migration for flow awkit-x48-no-such-flow.' with no channel name and a non-empty message (72/72, was 69/69).

New npm run verify:ipc-error-message (22/22, class unit) covers the reported string, narrowness (specific error names preserved, mid-message quotes untouched, no-wrapper messages unchanged), degenerate input, cause retention, and a source guard that exactly one direct ipcRenderer.invoke remains. Four mutations produce focused failures: preamble not stripped, any *Error: name stripped, unanchored match, one call site bypassing the wrapper.

Also repaired collateral damage the rename caused: verify:ipc-contract parsed preload for 'ipcRenderer.invoke("channel")' and dropped to '0 exposed, 224 backend-only'. It now accepts both spellings AND carries a cardinality floor, so a pattern that stops matching fails loudly instead of reporting an empty contract. 5/5, 202 exposed.
